summary: Forest Service lookout site on Bosque Peak, Manzano Mountains, NM; established 1911 with a telephone line; listed as gone; no source describes remains.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no date or cause given

access.note: Reached by hiking trail through the Manzano Mountains Wilderness; the high point is an off-trail venture

visit.trail_note: Bosque Peak Trail (174) rises steadily for the first mile and reaches the crest; the final stretch to the high point is off trail

events.note: Forest Service lookout site established; telephone line to the Tajique ranger station, per a July 1912 newspaper item
Supervisor said the station proved valuable in detecting incipient fires before much damage was done

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A July 1912 newspaper item calls the forest the Manzano national forest; the Forest Lookouts page now places the peak in the Cibola National Forest. The forest name changed; the land is the same.

notes_for_editor: The 1911 and 1912 events rest on one compiled page (Forest Lookouts) that quotes two newspaper items; the newspapers themselves were not read. The brief's record (Cibola NF, unknown type, gone) checks out; access is now known to be public trail access. No staffing, design, fire or removal information was found. The Wikipedia Bosque Peak article does not mention the lookout. Grokipedia says the station was established in 1911 but is AI-written and was not used. The cabin and Rea family link is unconfirmed and is not tied to the lookout in any source. The hiking group's page as we read it does not mention a cabin, though the 2017 blog says its report does; the cabin claim therefore rests on the blog alone.
